notes.decision: Single-letter line 11 'ⲡⲉ' read as the Coptic numeral ⲡ̄ⲉ̄ = 85, i.e. the chapter number for the new kephalaion 'Concerning the Cross of Light' that begins on line 12. This positioning (between paragraph break and chapter title) is consistent with chapter-numbering practice elsewhere in the Kephalaia.

Read ⲡⲉ ⲭⲉ as Lycopolitan ⲡⲉϫⲉ '(he) said' (Lyc ⲭ for ϫ), the standard Kephalaia chapter-opening formula. The lacuna conceals the speaker (likely 'the Apostle') and the introductory portion of the saying. The closing 'ϩⲱⲙ ⲡⲉ ⲁⲭⲱϩ' = 'the treading is upon him' parallels line 20 'ⲛⲉϩϩⲱⲙ ⲁⲭⲱϩ' — 'lest he tread upon him,' establishing the Cross-of-Light as that which is liable to being trodden underfoot.
ⲱⲛ rendered 'opened (his mouth) to' — Lycopolitan ⲟⲩⲱⲛ 'open,' standard idiom of Coptic dialogue introduction (cf. ⲟⲩⲱⲛ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉϥⲧⲁⲡⲣⲟ 'opened his mouth').
Read as Lycopolitan variant of ⲥϣⲉ 'it is fitting/right.' The construction ⲥⲱⲉ ⲁⲡⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲁⲧⲣⲉϩ-VERB matches the standard Coptic deontic ⲥϣⲉ ⲉ-PERSON ⲉ-VERB 'it is fitting for X to do Y.'

ⲣⲱⲧ rendered 'sprout' (a growing thing); ϩⲏⲡ qualitative 'hidden'; ⲛ̄ⲁⲣⲭⲏ 'in the beginning' — i.e., a seedling-stage hidden growth. The disciple's worry: that crushing such a sprout is destroying a Light-element in its earliest emergence.

Rendered 'creeping thing' per accumulated vocabulary entry ⲛⲝⲉⲧϩⲉ (Lyc ⲭ/ⲝ for ϫ = ϫⲁⲧϥⲉ 'creeping thing, reptile'). Fits the disciple's anxiety about treading on Light-bearing creatures alongside treading on the Cross of Light.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲙⲟⲩⲟⲩⲧ 'kill, slay' — with vowel shift and final ϩ for ⲧ.
Greek loanword αἰσθάνεσθαι 'perceive, sense.' First-person form 'perceiving (that...)' completing the participial chain ⲃⲓ...ⲧⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ ⲧⲣⲁⲓⲥⲑⲁⲛⲉ 'bearing... knowing... perceiving.'

ⲃⲣⲟ here in the sense 'triumph, victory' (cf. accumulated ⲃⲣⲟ 'joy/triumph,' confirmed by collocation with ⲛⲁⲃ 'great' = 'great triumph'). The disciple sees his charitable journey as a 'great triumph' — ecclesial-soteriological gain — yet fears the cost in trodden Light.
Read as ϯ-ⲣ̄-ϩⲁⲧⲉ '(I) am-afraid,' first-person present habitual idiom ⲣ̄ϩⲁⲧⲉ 'be afraid' (Lyc ⲡϩⲁⲧⲉ for ⲣϩⲁⲧⲉ).

Translated 'without strength in my head.' ⲁⲭⲛ̄ = 'without' (Sah. ⲁϫⲛ̄); ⲟⲁⲙ = Lyc. for ϫⲟⲙ 'strength/power' (cf. accumulated ⲛⲟⲁⲙ 'might/strength'); ⲧⲁⲟⲁⲡ = 'my head' (Lyc., cf. accumulated ⲡⲁⲁⲡⲉ 'head/sheaf'). The disciple is reporting his exhausted state on the journey, picked up again in line 28 where he says †ϩⲁϣϩⲱ ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲟⲁⲡ 'I afflict my head.'

Translated 'your Great-One who is over you.' ⲛⲁⲟ as substantive ('great one') here likely refers to the disciple's superior or commissioning master, parallel to 'what they have placed upon you' (ⲡⲉⲧⲭⲁⲩ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲕ) in next line. Could alternatively be 'your Great (matter)' as the great burden/charge laid upon him, but the personal reading better fits the institutional-apostolic register.

Translated 'tread with the soles of his foot.' ⲛⲟⲁⲡ tentatively read as Lyc. for the soles/under-parts of the foot; ϩⲡⲁⲟⲡⲟ as a treading/pressing verb fitting context. The whole clause expresses what he does upon ⲡⲥⲧⲁⲩⲣⲟⲥ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'the cross of Light' = the Living Soul mingled in matter that the apostle inevitably tramples in walking on the earth. Line 19 confirms: ⲉϥϩⲱⲙ ⲁⲭⲙ ⲡⲕⲁϩ ⲙ̄ⲛ ⲡⲥⲧⲁⲩⲣⲟⲥ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'treading upon the land and the cross of Light.'

Translated 'Destruction.' Lyc. form likely related to ⲧⲁⲕⲟ 'destroy/perish.' Paired with ⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ ('Sin') in 'the road of Sin and of Destruction' as the cosmic-soteriological doublet for the path of the self-willed traveler. Capitalized as cosmic principle paralleling capitalized Sin.

Translated 'wholly a kingship.' ⲟⲩⲟⲣⲟ likely from root ⲟⲩⲣⲟ/ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'king' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲟⲣⲟ, ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ). Parallel to line 16 ⲟⲩⲕⲗⲁⲙ ϩⲓ ⲃⲁⲉ ⲡⲉ ⲡⲉϥⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲧ ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ 'a crown and palm-branch is his entire road' — both name the victorious eschatological reward of the traveler-for-God's-sake. Alternative reading 'a joy' (ⲟⲩⲣⲟⲧ) is possible but less consistent with the 'crown'-imagery.

Translated 'I afflict.' Lyc. verb of pressing/wearying-down (cf. accumulated ⲡϩⲁⲱϩⲱ̄ 'wearying/wasting' as cognate). The disciple says 'I afflict my head' worrying over whether his trampling constitutes sin — the very anxiety the apostle is now resolving.

Translated 'the prior matter.' Compound ⲡⲣ̄ⲣ̄ϩⲁⲧⲉ = ⲡ-ⲣ̄-ⲣ̄ϩⲁⲧⲉ where ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix) + ϩⲁⲧⲉ ('front, before' = ϩⲏ) gives 'going-before, precedence' — substantivized as 'the prior (matter).' Functions as anaphoric referent to the topic addressed earlier. Cf. accumulated ⲡⲱⲣⲡ̄ϩⲁⲧⲉ in same field.
Translated 'shall reach' from ⲧⲉⲍⲟ 'reach, befall' (in glossary) + 3sg.m suffix; future ⲛⲁ-. The sickness 'reaches' the members (befalls them).
Greek loanword λύπη as a stative predicate: 'is in grief.' The article ⲡ̄- here functions predicatively in Lyc., similar to ⲣ̄-ⲗⲩⲧⲏ 'to grieve' (in glossary).
Qualitative/circumstantial 'being pricked' from ⲧⲕⲉⲥ 'sting, prick' (Lyc. = Sah. ⲧⲱⲕⲥ̄, in glossary as 'affliction'). Bodily-medical register: the soul is pricked in the sickness.

ⲧⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧ 'cheering of heart' — ⲧⲱⲕ here likely from ⲧⲱⲕ 'kindle, hearten, encourage' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'purpose of heart' but distinct root). The physician brings cheer (rallying of heart) to the sick.
Rendered 'his salvation/health' (Lyc. = Sah. ⲟⲩϫⲁⲓ 'health, salvation'). The medical-soteriological register fits: physician gives healing/salvation. Possessive ⲡ-ⲟⲩ-ⲭⲉⲓⲧⲉ 'his health.'
Translated 'has befallen him' — ⲛⲉⲍⲥⲉ as a verb of arrival/befalling (possibly Lyc. reflex of ⲛⲉϩⲥⲉ 'wake/come upon' in transferred sense). Confidence moderate.

Translated 'them, calling them' — parsing as object pronoun ⲙⲙⲟⲩ + verbal infinitive ⲧⲉⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ (or ⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'to call'); alternatively 'the names' (Lyc. plural). The wise man knows-them and calls-them physicians.
Substantival qualitative 'the suffering one' — ⲡⲉⲧ- + ϩⲁⲭ (possibly Lyc. for ϩⲱϫ 'be afflicted, oppressed'). The therapy is 'of the sufferer.'

Translated 'the names' — taking ⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ here as substantival 'naming/names' rather than infinitive. The physician declares the diagnostic names of the diseases. Alternative 'the gods' is grammatically possible but contextually unlikely.

Substantival 'the other examination' — ⲍⲱⲙ here functioning as a noun parallel to its verbal use throughout the chapter (lines 11, 15, 17, 20, 22, 26). Likely Lyc. reflex of a verb of close inspection/diagnosis (possibly cognate with Sah. ⲥⲱⲙ 'investigate' or ϫⲱⲱⲙⲉ).
Translated 'upon' — Lyc. reflex of ⲉϫⲛ̄ 'upon, over.' The physician's examination of what is upon (i.e. visible in/on) the members.

Rendered 'remove from him' — Lyc. ⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲟ likely from ⲧⲟⲩⲱ/ⲧⲟⲩⲟ 'send forth, expel' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise' — here in horizontal-expulsion sense). The physician removes the sickness from the patient.

Translated 'and to bring forth this profit' — ⲧⲁⲗⲁⲓⲟ̄ⲉ as Lyc. causative 'cause to come up, bring forth' (cf. ⲧⲁⲗⲟ 'mount, raise'). The physician's purpose: to produce profit (ⲡⲍⲏⲩ in glossary) for the sick man.
Translated 'bring forth wrath' — ⲭⲡⲟ (Lyc. ϫⲡⲟ 'beget, bring forth') + ⲛⲉⲟ̈ⲉ 'wrath/anger' (likely Lyc. reflex of ⲛⲟⲩϭⲥ̄ or related anger-noun). Pair-partner with ⲃⲗⲕⲉ 'anger' (line 27 doublet).
Translated 'treachery/plot' — Greek ἐπιβουλία 'plot, malicious design' rendered with Lyc. orthography. Fits the context of the hostile examiner who wishes to add another sickness.

Lexeme uncertain. Tentative reading 'with cover/concealment' or 'under malice'; possibly ϩⲁ- 'under' + ⲃⲓⲱⲡ (root unidentified — possibly cognate with ⲃⲱⲡ 'cover' or related). Left in Coptic in the rendering pending parallel attestations.

Rendered 'the other face' — ⲍⲟ = Lyc. ϩⲟ 'face' (cf. ⲡⲍⲟ in glossary). In this paraphrase of Matt 6:21 ('where your treasure is, there your heart will be'), the saying may be reformulated reciprocally with 'the other face/aspect' substituted for 'treasure.' Alternative reading 'the other treasure' (ⲍⲟ as Lyc. for ⲁϩⲟ) is also possible.

Translated 'to the King' — Lyc. ⲡⲟⲣⲟ = Sah. ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'king' (cf. accumulated ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ, ⲡⲓⲣⲡⲟ). The diaeresis ⲟ̈ marks the spelling. The bones afflicted are drawn 'to the King' — to the divine kingship, soteriological terminus.

Reduplicative emphatic phrase across the line break: 'this labor — labor again of the other bones.' ⲍⲁϣ likely = Lyc. for affliction/labor (possibly cognate with ⲍⲱϣ 'afflict' attested in line 30 ⲁⲕⲍⲉϣⲍⲱϣϩ). Rendering both occurrences as 'labor' to preserve the iteration.

Translated 'transgressor / transgressing word' on the basis of the recurring opposition with ⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sin' (line 15) and the parallel construction ⲣⲉⲣⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sinner' in the corpus. The verb ⲱⲱⲃⲉ characterizes a word/act that 'harms the cross of light' (l.6) and produces demons (l.16). Likely Lycopolitan reflex of a verb of transgression/blame — possibly cognate with ⲱⲡ in the sense 'be charged/accused' or with ⲟⲩⲱⲃⲉ 'oppose.' Confidence moderate.

Tentatively rendered 'the foremost matter' analyzing as ⲡⲱⲣⲡ̄ (= ϣⲟⲣⲡ 'first') + ϩⲁⲧⲉ (cf. ϩⲏ 'front, before'). Alternative readings include 'previously' or 'matter mentioned before.' Functions as a discourse-marker linking back to a prior topic. Confidence low.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲥⲉⲭⲉ ⲛⲃⲁⲗ ⲙⲛ ⲡⲁⲧⲃⲗⲁⲕⲉ ⲙⲛ ⲡⲁⲧⲭⲟⲗⲏ
notes.decision: Rendered 'the word of the (evil) eye with that-of-wrath and that-of-gall.' ⲥⲉⲭⲉ ⲛⲃⲁⲗ literally 'word of eye' = malicious/envious utterance (cf. evil eye idiom). ⲡⲁⲧⲃⲗⲁⲕⲉ analyzed as ⲡⲁ-(ⲧ-)ⲃⲗⲁⲕⲉ 'the one of wrath' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲃⲗ̄ⲕⲉ 'wrath'); ⲡⲁⲧⲭⲟⲗⲏ 'the one of gall' (Greek χολή). Three-fold catalogue of the venomous-speech vices.

Rendered 'malice indeed.' ⲕⲁⲕⲁϩ likely a Lycopolitan reduplicated form related to ⲕⲱϩ 'envy, jealousy' or to ⲕⲁⲕⲓⲁ 'evil.' ⲙⲙⲉⲧⲉ taken as adverbial 'in truth, indeed' (cf. Sah ⲛⲁⲙⲉ). Alternative reading: ⲕⲁⲕⲁϩ 'discord' + ⲙⲙⲉⲧⲉ 'agreement' = 'malicious agreement.' Confidence low.

Rendered 'shall plot against' analyzing as future ⲛⲁ- + verb ⲥⲁⲣϥ̄ (possibly Lyc. for ⲥⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'ruin, demolish' or ⲥⲱⲣ 'spread/scatter' with 3sg.m suffix). The construction ⲥⲁⲣϥ ⲥⲁ ⲡⲉϥⲥⲁⲛ 'against his brother' fits a hostile-speech action consistent with the surrounding catalogue of accusatorial sins. Alternative: 'shall slander.' Confidence low.

Rendered 'wise physician.' ⲥⲉⲓ̈ⲛⲉ = Lyc. for ⲥⲁⲉⲓⲛ 'physician.' The medical-soteriological simile structures the closing portion: the righteous teacher's word is to the soul what the wise physician's surgical-pharmacological treatment (cutting, cleansing, applying corrosive medicine, burning, piercing) is to the body — apparent harm that effects healing. Standard Manichaean trope.

Rendered 'the iron' (already in glossary). Here used in surgical-metaphorical sense: 'burn her in the iron and pierce her' = cauterizing iron applied to the wounded soul/matter. Direct correspondential continuity with the bitter-tree / iron-body register of earlier kephalaia: the iron now becomes the redemptive instrument when wielded by the wise physician (= righteous apostle).

Translated 'medicine.' Lyc. reflex of ⲡⲁϩⲣⲉ 'medicine, drug' (already attested in accumulated vocabulary as ⲡⲗⲅⲟ/ⲧⲗⲅⲟ 'healing'). The structuring image of this kephalaion is medical: bitter medicine + scraping + harsh treatment, all accepted by the patient because of the cure.
Translated 'the sick.' Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡϣⲱⲛⲉ 'the sick one'; confirmed by parallel ⲡⲓⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲉⲧϣⲱⲛⲉ 'the sick man' in line 3 and ⲡⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲉⲧϣ[ⲱⲛⲉ] in line 13.

Translated 'the bitter medicine.' ⲕⲏⲃ likely Lyc. for ⲕⲱⲃⲉ/ⲥⲓϣⲉ 'be bitter' or related; pairs naturally with the ⲡⲁⲍⲣⲉ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲱⲙ 'medicines that are eaten' of line 1, contrasting bitter (oral?) treatment with the pleasanter draughts.

Translated 'and scrapes.' Likely conjunctive from ⲥⲕⲁⲓ/ⲥⲕⲁϩⲕⲉϩ 'scrape, abrade' (cf. accumulated ⲕⲁⲍⲕⲍ 'scraping/abrading' in surgical-treatment register). Fits the medical-procedural inventory of bitter medicine + scraping + foul-thing within.

Translated 'Sin.' Read as Lycopolitan vowel-variant of ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sin' (in glossary); the construction ⲙⲁϩⲭⲡⲟ ⲛⲉⲃⲉ ⲍⲙ ⲡⲉϥⲍⲏⲧ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲣⲁϥ 'begetting of Sin in his heart against him' is a classic Coptic moral-psychological formula. Capitalized per terminology guide for cosmic principle.

Translated tentatively 'the cutting ... the foul-thing.' Both lexemes are obscure. ⲡⲟⲩⲱⲭⲉ taken as Lyc. variant of ⲡⲱϫⲉ/ⲟⲩⲱϫⲉ 'split, cut, break' — fitting a surgical incision in the medical parable. ⲡⲧⲭⲟⲩϥ (with ⲧ-prefix) tentatively related to ϫⲱϥ/ϫⲱϩⲙ̄ 'foul, defiled' or ϫⲱϥⲧ̄ — the unpleasant substance the doctor places within the wound. Both flagged as low-confidence.
Translated 'which he opens (it).' Tentatively parsed as relative + future + ⲟⲩⲱⲡϫ̄/ⲟⲩⲱϫⲃ̄ 'open, lay bare' with 3sg.m object. Could alternatively be ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ̄ 'answer.' Confidence low.
Translated 'in other wages.' ⲃⲉⲕⲏⲩⲉ is a Lyc. plural of ⲃⲉⲕⲉ 'wages, recompense' with ⲕⲉ- 'other.' Standard Coptic formation for reciprocal payment.

Translated 'his form.' Lyc. ⲍⲙⲁⲧ = ⲥⲙⲟⲧ 'form, fashion, manner' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ for the same root with article-variation). Here = the doctor's character/form which the patient takes on in becoming his lifelong friend.

Translated 'the man... the elect one.' The parable's exegetical move: the elect IS the physician; Mercy IS the sick patient. Standard Manichaean correspondential identification — direct, not analogical.

Translated 'she shall purify him in the icon of the holy ones.' ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ here read as ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄/ⲥⲱⲧⲃ̄ 'choose, purify' with 3sg.m object — Mercy purifies the elect through her icon (= the visible sanctity of the saints). Alternative reading 'redeem him' also possible.
Translated 'consuming her.' ⲟⲩⲱ here read as Lyc. for ⲟⲩⲱⲙ 'eat, consume.' Standard Manichaean motif: the Living Soul / Mercy is consumed and afflicted in the cosmos before being released.
Translated 'her gate of going forth.' ⲣⲟ 'gate, mouth' + possessive ⲡⲉⲥ- + 'of going-forth.' The toil and grief of the elect IS the gate through which Mercy goes forth out of the cosmos.
Translated 'the examination.' Greek σκέψις, already in accumulated vocabulary. Functions here as the first of the enumerated ascetic-monastic virtues required of the elect.

Translated tentatively 'the simplicity.' Possibly a Lycopolitan/scribal rendering of Greek ἁπλότης 'simplicity, sincerity' (with consonantal metathesis), fitting the catalogue of monastic virtues here. Alternative: ἀψυχία 'lifelessness/dispassion.' Confidence low.
Translated 'the continence.' Greek ἐγκράτεια — standard ascetic virtue of self-mastery, especially sexual continence. Lyc. ⲧⲉⲣ- for ἐγκρ-.
Translated 'the only-begottenness.' Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ- + Greek μονογενής. In Manichaean ascetic register denotes the celibate/single state of the elect (not Christological 'only-begotten').
Translated 'the anchoritism.' Greek ἀναχώρησις — withdrawal/anchoritic life. Standard monastic virtue.

Translated 'the gifts.' Reads as Coptic indefinite plural ⲛ̄- + ϣⲥⲛ̄- (uncertain prefix) + δωρεαί 'gifts.' Could alternatively be a different Greek loan; the dwelling of δωρεαί among ascetic virtues fits the inventory.
Translated 'the asceticism of bonds.' Greek ἄσκησις + Coptic ⲙⲣ̄ⲣⲉ 'bonds' (in glossary). The ascetic discipline of bound vows — standard Manichaean elect-discipline.
Translated 'the land of the Living.' Greek χώρα 'land, region' + Lyc. plural participle 'those who live.' Standard Manichaean designation for the eschatological abode of the redeemed.

Greek πρὸς ὥραν 'for an hour, temporary' contrasts with Coptic ϣⲁ ⲁⲛⲏϩⲉ 'unto eternity.' Standard Manichaean/Pauline soteriological antithesis (cf. 2 Cor 4:17): the brief affliction of the catechumen-life produces eternal rest among the saints.

'The Living Cross' = the Cross of Light (cf. ⲡⲥⲧⲁⲩⲣⲟⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ in glossary), the Living Soul mingled in matter, especially in the alms-food. To eat in luxury is to profane this Cross. ϣⲱⲃⲉ ⲁ- here = 'turn (it) toward, exchange (it) for' — the disciplined Living Cross is being converted into a luxurious feast.
Imperative pl. of ⲣⲉϩⲭⲁⲩⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲧ 'guide, path-setter' (in glossary). The elect are commanded to be guides (for her = the soul/community) in the speech to the catechumens.

3sg.f. subject 'she exists in great affliction.' Antecedent unstated but contextually = the Living Soul (ⲯⲩⲭⲏ fem.) bound in the food, awaiting liberation through the elect's disciplined eating. Standard Manichaean ritual cosmology.
Lyc verb of approach/intent: 'when you go/draw near (to eat).' Could also be intentional 'when you wish to eat,' but motion-toward-action sense fits the ritual context.

Reduplicated ⲭⲡ̄ⲭⲡ̄ rendered 'tippling/gulping' (gulping repeatedly); ⲭⲏⲣ tentatively 'carousing/revelry' as a vice in the eating-discipline list paired with luxury and drunkenness. Etymology of ⲭⲏⲣ uncertain.

ⲣⲁⲩϣ = Coptic 'care, concern' (Crum 308a). 'Bear the care of your body by means of her' = sustain the body through the disciplined alms-meal — the body is supported by the very food in which the Living Soul is contained.

'You alone are without sin therein' — only the elect, eating in this disciplined manner, is sinless in the consumption; the catechumens who prepare the food may bear sin (since their hands have plucked/cut), but the elect's discipline absolves the consumption itself. Manichaean ritual logic.

Lyc abstract = 'gentleness, lightness of heart' — paired here with ⲡⲟⲩⲣⲁⲧ ⲙ̄ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ 'joy of the Mind' (line 31) as the inner state produced by Mani's teaching. Not standard ⲙⲛⲧϩⲁⲣϣ-ϩⲏⲧ 'patience'; ϩⲁⲗⲃⲏⲧ here functions as 'gentle/calm of heart.'
